item.title: Disneyland, actors' union clash over parental leave, benefits as union negotiates first contract
item.description: A newly formed union for Disneyland's performers is in tense negotiations with Disney as employees struggle to get by in one of America's most expensive states.
item.content:encoded:
Magic United, an affiliate of Actors' Equity representing 1,700 parade, show and character cast members at Disneyland, and Disney are in the midst of negotiations on a first contract, and they're telling Fox News Digital it's not going smoothly.

While most Disneyland employees have been represented by unions for decades, the Characters and Parades department remained nonunion until workers voted to organize in 2024 amid California’s cost-of-living crisis after the pandemic. This has led to negotiations between the newly formed union and Disney in order to negotiate a first contract both parties can agree on.

Because this is the workers' first union contract, both sides disagree over how to characterize Disney's proposals. Disney argues it is negotiating the initial terms of employment rather than eliminating existing union benefits. The union counters that workers currently receive benefits such as paid parental leave, so excluding them from the first contract would effectively mean employees lose those benefits.

The Los Angeles Times noted that, "Although the union said it has been getting movement on a number of health and safety issues, there are other points in contention, including the amount the company matches for employee contributions to their 401(k) retirement savings plans and a proposal that limits the number of times a worker can give away a shift without managerial approval."

DISNEYLAND MAY SCRAP LONG-STANDING PARK RULE THAT FRUSTRATED VISITORS

Fox News Digital contacted both parties about the ongoing negotiations, recalling founder Walt Disney’s famous anecdote about having founded the Disneyland park as a place where parents and their children can have fun together, asking whether Disney is fulfilling that mission as negotiations continue.

"Disneyland is often presented as ‘the ultimate family-friendly destination,’ but that’s no longer the case for 1,700 Cast Members in the Characters and Parades departments who create Disney magic by bringing beloved characters to life in shows, meet and greets and character dining experiences," a representative for the union responded.

"Disney has proposed eliminating paid parental leave for these workers and in the first year of a contract the company presented a zero percent wage increase – despite a period of high inflation. Orange County, California where Disneyland is located also is rated as one of the costliest places to live in the United States," the spokesperson added.

The representative claimed further that Disneyland "wants to eliminate paid parental leave, cut the number of paid holidays and size of401(k) contributions and make it unnecessarily harder for Character and Parade workers to swap shifts."

Al Vincent Jr., Actors’ Equity’s Executive Director, told the Los Angeles Times in a report about these negotiations, "When you propose to take away paid parental leave from those who work day in and day out to give other families great experiences, that’s not family friendly."

CHEAPEST DAYS TO VISIT DISNEY: HERE'S WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW BEFORE BOOKING YOUR TRIP

Jessica Jakary, a Disneyland Resort spokesperson, has contested these claims, declaring to Fox News Digital, "Disneyland Resort values its cast members, offers competitive benefits and is proud of its long history of working collaboratively with the unions that represent them."

Disney as a company has stated that it is committed to ongoing negotiations with Magic United, noting to Fox News that there appears to be some confusion in the comparison to Walt Disney World in Florida where there are no state disability payments for parental leave like those provided for in California.

Disney has also said to Fox News Digital that it has not proposed to limit the ability to trade shifts, but instead the proposal only limits the number of times a cast member can give away a shift without managerial approval.

Disney also said that Disneyland Resort has proposed wage increases over the term of the agreement, and that while it is not offering an immediate wage increase, it has continued to provide annual increases to this bargaining unit as negotiations progress.

In one example provided, Disney claims that as of December 2025, full-time and part-time cast members in this bargaining unit have received a 4% increase.

item.title: Primary showdown: Polls close in Tennessee as conservative firebrand eyes governor's office
item.description: Marsha Blackburn leads Tennessee's Republican gubernatorial primary despite Trump staying neutral, while key congressional races reshape the state's map.
item.content:encoded:
The polls have closed in Tennessee as conservative firebrand Sen. Marsha Blackburn aims to change her work address from Washington D.C., to Nashville.

The former longtime congresswoman and two-term senator with a robust national profile thanks to her regular cable news appearances is considered the front-runner in Thursday's Republican gubernatorial primary, in the race to succeed term-limited GOP Gov. Bill Lee.

The Republican face-off for governor of Tennessee, where Democrats haven't won a gubernatorial election in two decades, takes top billing as the red-leaning southeastern state holds nominating contests for state and federal offices.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Blackburn is running in a race that also includes four-term Rep. John Rose, who like Blackburn is a staunch Capitol Hill supporter of President Donald Trump, and state Rep. Monty Fritts.

Even though the president handed out endorsements in other GOP gubernatorial primaries this cycle, Trump remained neutral in the Tennessee contest.

"Unfortunately, she’s running for governor. She’s running for governor of Tennessee. I’d love her not to, I begged her," Trump said in January. "‘I said, ‘Marsha, don’t. We don’t want to lose you in the Senate.’"

But the president has said Blackburn would be a good governor, and also noted that Rose has been a staunch loyalist.

Even though she didn't land Trump's endorsement, Blackburn has showcased her support for him.

"As President Trump sends power and authority back to the states, I'm ready to deliver for the people of the Volunteer State and make our state America's conservative leader," she wrote on the eve of the primary in a social media post that included a photo of her and Trump.

Five Democrats, including Memphis City Councilwoman Jerri Green, are bidding for their party's gubernatorial nomination.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Tennessee's other U.S. senator, Republican Bill Hagerty, is unopposed in the GOP primary as he seeks a second six-year term in the Senate.

Five Democrats are vying to challenge Hagerty in the general election. Then-Sen. Al Gore's re-election 36 years ago was the last time a Democrat won a Senate contest in Tennessee.

In U.S. House battles, Memphis voters will cast ballots for their Democratic and Republican nominees using a new GOP-drawn congressional district map that created an extra right-leaning seat and forced longtime Democratic Rep. Steve Cohen to not seek re-election.

Meanwhile, two-term Republican Rep. Andy Ogles, a major Trump ally in the House who is backed by the president, is facing a stiff primary challenge from Tennessee Agriculture Commissioner Charlie Hatcher, who was endorsed earlier this week by Lee. The race has seen a large infusion of money from outside groups.

item.title: Sam Acho Q&A: Former NFL player and ESPN analyst speaks out on civility and accountability in sports and media
item.description: Sam Acho explains how NFL locker room debates can be a model for civil discourse and why athletes should use their platforms to speak up with integrity.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL player and current ESPN NFL analyst Sam Acho attended the Ronald Reagan Foundation Center on Civility & Democracy’s inaugural Reagan Civility & Democracy Forum last week.

There, he advocated for improving civility among Americans, especially in sports.

"We talked about civility in sports and how many of the same attributes athletes use can be applied to civil discourse: sportsmanship, winning and losing the right way, and playing within a set of rules," Acho told Fox News Digital.

PATRIOTS LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI REVEALS THE IMPACT POLITICS HAS ON LOCKER ROOM DYNAMICS

As a former pro athlete and now a top sports media figure, Acho shared his vision for the role of athletes and sports media in promoting civility across the country, and how Sophie Cunningham fits into it, in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital.

Questions and answers have been shortened for brevity and focus.

Q: What does civil discourse look like to you?

Sam Acho: It can include disagreement. You don’t always have to be on the same page. In football, some people believe in a 3-4 defense; others prefer a 4-3. Some say you have to blitz to get to the quarterback... others believe in playing coverage... but the goal is the same: to win the game.

In society — especially among political leaders — the goal should be to serve the country and make it better... People may disagree about which law or approach is best, but at the end of the day, it’s about wanting the country to be better.

Q: Did conversations about politics and other issues happen in NFL locker rooms?

Sam Acho: Nowhere in the locker room was it not allowed to have certain conversations...

We'd have debates about, um, is it harder to, to be a track athlete or a golfer.

We'd also have political debates. We'd talk about politics, talk about certain rules, certain laws. "Hey, what do we think about what the president said? What do we think about what this governor is trying to do?"

... I remember we were, when Colin Kaepernick was taking a knee and protesting during the national anthem, we weren't shying away from that.

Q: Did those conversations ever become uncivil?

Sam Acho: In any family, in any team, in any conversation, you may cross the line, but usually when you cross the line, you either apologize or they apologize, or you try to find a way to make it right.

I'm not, I'm not gonna pretend that we lived in a utopia... But when you cross the line or when you go out of bounds or when you make a mistake, okay, you either apologize, or when you lose, right, you shake hands, you move on, right?

When the conversations did become uncivil, or maybe we had a big disagreement, I didn't drop my ball and walk away. No, I actually went and said, "Oh, we have practice in like 15 minutes." Then we had meetings in two hours. Then we were together at lunch the next day.

Q: How could the NFL and its players, coaches and executives help promote civility?

Sam Acho: I think one thing that athletes have that many other people don't is a platform. A lot of athletes have a platform... And I think one area that quarterbacks, that coaches, that players, that athletes can continue to use is their platform, not only to speak out on issues that matter to them, but also to educate themselves on issues that matter.

And so one area I think that athletes... and coaches and executives can do is to continue to speak up and, and stay educated on topics.

Q: Do you believe using that platform to speak up on topics comes with the risk of promoting uncivil discourse?

Sam Acho: Everything comes with risk. Life comes with risk... But oftentimes it's not really about risk, it's more about... how do you respond to defeat? How do you respond to adversity? How do you respond to, uh, something not going your way?

When I'm on TV... there's a risk that people may disagree with my opinion, but that doesn't mean that I just absolve myself from the conversation. It's understanding the risk... and still moving forward with an educated perspective.

Q: But in general, you would encourage more athletes, especially those with platforms, to make their feelings on certain topics known?

Sam Acho: I would encourage athletes to continue to understand that they are more than just what you do on a field. That's probably my biggest encouragement. Oftentimes... you, as an athlete, you think that, or people tell you that you are what you put on tape.

That you're only that, and you're more than just that. There's our human capital. There's your physical capital. Yes, you train, you eat right, you go to sleep on time to be the best athlete you can be. But there's also your intellectual capital.

KATIE UHLAENDER: ATHLETES RISK PAYING THE PRICE IF PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT IS PASSED

Athletes should know they are more than one dimension of a human being. The same is true for people in politics: You are more than a governor or a senator. You should ask who you are becoming as you make decisions. Are you simply trying to gather as much power as possible, or do you recognize that there is something beyond one election or one vote?

Q: What do you think about Sophie Cunningham’s recent use of her platform?

Sam Acho: So I'd have to get, I'd have to dial myself back more in to see what kind of what Sophie Cunningham has been saying and not saying, but I will say, I go back to this. Like, as an athlete, you have an opportunity to use your platform and to steward it well. You absolutely do.

And I don't think that athletes should shy away from speaking up for what they believe. I think so many people in society, they speak up for what they believe. And know that, yeah, there's a risk involved for sure. I think that athletes should continue to use and to steward their platform, knowing that you may not be liked you may not be liked, but I think athletes should continue to use their platform and steward it well.

Q: How can sports media figures do a better job of promoting civil discourse?

Sam Acho: It goes back to the idea of platform. A lot of sports media figures, not all, but many were former athletes. So they put down that physical side, now they're using the intellectual side.

And I think it is remembering that even as a sports media, media figure, you do have a platform. Pat McAfee has a huge platform on ESPN. I think about, um, and what he's been able to do with his platform, and then using that to realize that people follow you. People listen to you. People may not agree with everything you say, but you do have a platform, and you want to steward it well.

Your voice, your opinion, those things are yours. So they're yours to steward. They're not yours to say, "Okay, how can I gather as much power, as many followers as I can?" And just waste it. No, you're a steward.

Q: What does it look like to steward a sports media platform poorly?

Sam Acho: There was a game last year, last season, or maybe the season before, and Texas played Georgia. And third quarter of the game or so, late third quarter, there was a call that didn't go Texas's way. Texas was the home team. They were hosting Georgia. And a lot of the fans were upset the referees missed the call. Well, while the referees missed the call, all of a sudden the fans at Texas started to throw cans and, and bottles and things on the field in order to delay the game so that the referees could go and maybe look at the call and try and reverse the call.

And the referees did end up going and changing the call. Texas still lost the game, No. 1. No. 2, it wasn't a good look for, uh, it wasn't a good look for Texas, and I think it's even being willing to say that, right? Not just saying, "Well, look, I went there and I'm a broadcaster and we won or we lost or they got the call right." No, the call was wrong, but you don't go and say, "I'm gonna just throw bottles on the field," and say that that's okay. I think that no matter who you are in sports and sports media and, and no matter what avenue you have, I think it's wise to say, "Hey, that was wrong. He was out of bounds.

"We were out of bounds." And, and realizing that it may cost you the game. And even if you try to, even if you do that thing that was wrong and, and, and, uh, you get the call that goes in your favor, what did you actually win??

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Michigan House speaker calls for answers over $300M taxpayer-funded Rx Kids program
item.description: Michigan House Republicans cut future funding for Rx Kids after questioning its voter registration ties and payments to undocumented recipients.
item.content:encoded:
The Republican leader of Michigan’s House says a state-funded maternal health initiative has become something far different than lawmakers were promised, accusing Democrats of using more than $300 million in taxpayer funding to advance a broader guaranteed-income agenda.

Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall made the remarks in an interview with Fox News Digital as House Republicans continue scrutinizing Rx Kids, a taxpayer-funded program that provides unrestricted cash payments to pregnant women and new mothers.

Hall argued lawmakers believed they were funding a maternal and prenatal health initiative, not what he described as a broader experiment in guaranteed income.

GUARANTEED INCOME PROGRAM TARGETS LOW-INCOME HOMES LED BY BLACK MOMS AS CASH HANDOUTS SURGE NATIONWIDE

"I think the Democrats kind of slipped this in here under the idea that it was for prenatal care," Hall told Fox News Digital. "Lawmakers did not have the complete picture."

Rx Kids launched in Flint in 2024 and provides expectant mothers with a $1,500 lump-sum payment during pregnancy, followed by $500 monthly payments after the child is born.

According to materials provided to Fox News Digital by Hall’s office, the program has expanded to communities across Michigan with more than $300 million in taxpayer funding.

Rx Kids has promoted the initiative as a maternal and infant health program designed to reduce financial stress for new families. According to podcast interviews and program materials, its leaders have also discussed expanding the model to communities across Michigan and beyond.

EXCLUSIVE: VIDEO SHOWS MICHIGAN LAWMAKER TOURING DAYCARE IN $1.1M TAXPAYER FUNDING PROBE

Hall argued the program lacks the eligibility requirements found in traditional public assistance programs.

"We have a lot of social safety net programs in our country that are working very well," Hall said. "They have eligibility checks. They look at citizenship. They look at income verification.

"Rx Kids, by design, is given to anyone that has a child," he continued. "They don’t look for citizenship. They just pay out anyone that has a child."

Hall’s office also provided Fox News Digital with video of legislative committee testimony in which program officials acknowledged payments had been made to individuals who were not legally present in the United States.

CALIFORNIA ‘BASIC INCOME’ EXPERIMENT FAILS TO PROVIDE ‘FINANCIAL INDEPENDENCE,’ STUDY FINDS

Hall argued taxpayer-funded cash assistance should include income and legal status requirements similar to those used by existing public assistance programs.

"What we prefer are the traditional welfare programs like Medicaid, the food stamp program and the WIC program," Hall said. "They make sure you’re here legally, they make sure you’re not making a lot of money and then they give you the benefit. That’s not what Rx Kids is."

Hall also criticized the program’s unrestricted cash payments, noting recipients are not required to spend the money on diapers, formula, housing or other expenses related to pregnancy or caring for a newborn.

"They give you this free cash and there are no strings attached by definition," Hall said.

MAYORS WANT TO KEEP HANDING OUT FREE CASH AFTER FEDERAL FUNDS DRIED UP

Hall said caseworkers had told him they had seen recipients use the money for alcohol, drugs and gambling. Fox News Digital has not independently verified those claims.

The speaker also pointed to public comments from Rx Kids leaders that he said reinforced Republican concerns that the initiative is intended to become something larger than a maternal health program.

Hall's office also shared podcast interviews in which Rx Kids co-founder Luke Shaefer discussed the expanded Child Tax Credit and the role he believes Rx Kids can play following the expiration of those federal payments.

In a separate interview, Dr. Mona Hanna, the leader of Rx Kids, discussed her vision of expanding the initiative into a government-scale public program.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED RECOUNTS SMASHING VODKA BOTTLE AFTER BEARD CRITICISM

Hall said those remarks aligned with his assessment of Rx Kids.

"This is a progressive left-wing experiment toward basically a universal income," Hall said. "They’re trying to move the welfare state down that lane."

Hall also questioned the program’s advisory network.

Hall's office also shared archived versions of the Rx Kids website that listed Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan Secretary of State and Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson's husband Ryan Friedrichs and Community Change official Dorian Warren as members of the program's advisory circle.

MICHIGAN’S TOP ELECTION OFFICIAL WINS DEMOCRATIC PRIMARY FOR GOVERNOR, ADVANCES TO BATTLEGROUND RACE

The advisory circle page was removed from the organization’s website days after lawmakers questioned program leaders during a June 2 Michigan House Oversight Committee hearing.

The timing of the removal does not establish why the page was taken down.

"Our secretary of state’s husband is on the advisory board. Abdul El-Sayed is on the board," Hall said. "It’s like a who’s who of radical left Democrats."

Hall’s office also pointed to an Rx Kids white paper examining voter turnout among recipients and the program’s promotion of Vot-ER, a physician-backed voter registration organization powered by TurboVote.

Materials provided by Hall’s office also identified Hanna as an adviser to Vot-ER.

Hall said those connections and the program’s research into voting behavior deserved additional scrutiny.

"We’re trying to understand why are you so interested in the voting pattern of the people that are receiving your no-strings-attached welfare," Hall said. "We aren’t getting good answers."

Hall said House Republicans did not include additional funding for Rx Kids in Michigan’s newly signed budget, though the program still has access to previously appropriated funds.

TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS

"The good news is that we cut off funding to this program in the new budget," Hall said. "In the future, we’re going to try to put guardrails around it so that it goes to the people that truly need it."

Rather than eliminating assistance for struggling families, Hall said he wants taxpayer dollars directed toward existing programs that assess financial need and place restrictions on how certain benefits can be spent.

"I think people support those programs," Hall said. "They have eligibility requirements to ensure that you’re not taking advantage of the system."

Fox News Digital reached out to Gov. Gretchen Whitmer’s office, Rx Kids and Michigan State University for comment.

item.title: Cruise line's tougher booking rules ignite backlash over higher deposits and payments
item.description: Princess Cruises is raising deposits and moving final payment deadlines to 120 days before departure, sparking online debate among travelers.
item.content:encoded:
Princess Cruises is introducing stricter booking policies, including higher deposits and earlier final payment deadlines, fueling mixed reactions among travelers.

Among the biggest changes is an update to the timeline for final payments, the cruise line confirmed in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Beginning with new bookings for sailings departing in 2027 and beyond, we are implementing a 120-day final payment and a modified cancellation fee schedule," the company said.

ANGRY CRUISE PASSENGERS BLAST MAJOR LINE OVER SURPRISE DAILY GRATUITY HIKE

"These changes bring greater consistency to the booking process and reflect broader industry practices, while also helping ensure that guests have fair access to the staterooms and sailings they want to experience."

The new rules take effect Sept. 2 for new bookings on sailings departing Jan. 1, 2027, or later. Guests were notified of the policy changes in an email from the cruise line, according to industry website Cruise Critic.

The cruise line is also increasing standard deposits. Guests booking seven-day cruises in inside, oceanview, balcony and mini-suite staterooms will now pay $300 per person, up from $250, while suite deposits will increase from $500 to $600 per person, according to the review website.

Princess Cruises also noted that reservations will automatically be canceled if final payment is not received by the deadline, though guests will continue receiving payment reminders before the due date, according to reports.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The policy changes have prompted debate among cruise fans on social media. Some travelers said the earlier deadlines will not affect their vacation plans because they typically pay off cruises as soon as possible.

"I pay it all as soon as I book," one person wrote on TikTok. "I get my reservations in that day, and I'm always sail ready."

Another commenter said, "I don't mind these changes because I like to pay off my trips as fast as I can so that I'm able to begin saving for the next one."

Others, however, questioned why passengers would be required to put down more money earlier in the booking process.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Those deposits are crazy," one commenter wrote.

Another person argued that the earlier payment deadline could create problems for travelers using payment plans.

"120 days out for final payment is the worst of all of it!" the commenter wrote. "Especially people who are on payment plans."

The booking changes come as other cruise lines have also introduced policies that have frustrated some travelers.

Fox News Digital previously reported that Celebrity Cruises faced backlash after raising its automatic gratuity charges with little notice, prompting some passengers to say they would tip crew members directly in cash instead.

The cruise line increased its daily automatic gratuities by $1.50 per person across all stateroom categories, raising the charges to between $19.50 and $24.50 per guest, per day.

Many passengers criticized the timing of the announcement, saying they were notified the same day the higher rates took effect.

"At this point, they just need to include gratuities in their fare like the luxury lines do," one Reddit user wrote.

item.title: Rams have assembled a roster to ruin football, just like the Dodgers have ruined baseball
item.description: Colin Cowherd claims the Los Angeles Rams have assembled the best NFL roster in at least a decade, and the case for an even bolder claim exists.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are overwhelming favorites to win the 2026 World Series. Most sportsbooks list their championship odds at around +150, implying roughly a 40% chance of winning the title, which would mark their third straight.

Aside from Dodgers fans, no serious observer can argue that one team having odds that high before the playoffs even begin is healthy for the sport.

Even before the Dodgers added reigning Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal to what was already baseball's best pitching rotation, the only compelling case against them winning another title was something random occurring.

THE LEFT WANTS CAITLIN CLARK, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TO SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE WHEN IT COMES TO TRANS SPORTS

Put simply, there is no logical baseball argument that another team is equipped to beat them in a postseason series.

No, the team's current six-game losing streak is not cause for concern. The Dodgers lost seven straight last July and still went 9-1 in the National League postseason.

The Dodgers have taken much of the suspense out of the baseball season by assembling a roster that is so far ahead of the competition. For most fans, that is discouraging.

A similar dynamic could emerge with another Los Angeles team, this one in the NFL.

On Wednesday, Fox Sports Radio host Colin Cowherd claimed that the Los Angeles Rams have assembled the best NFL roster in at least a decade. It's hard to disagree.

Last season, the Rams and the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks separated themselves from the rest of the league in most meaningful statistical categories. Since then, Seattle has lost several key contributors, including Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. Meanwhile, the Rams added cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, along with defensive end Myles Garrett.

For context, Garrett is widely considered the best defensive player in football. Garrett set the single-season sack record with 23 just last year. McDuffie is routinely ranked among the NFL's five best cornerbacks, while Watson is arguably the league's top No. 2 corner.

And, like the Dodgers, the Rams are not finished adding.

Nearly every prominent NFL reporter expects Aaron Donald to come out of retirement and rejoin Los Angeles before the season begins.

In case anyone has forgotten, Donald is one of the most dominant defensive players of the past 30 years. He is perhaps the greatest defensive tackle in NFL history.

The only reason Garrett is not universally considered the greatest defensive player of his era is that Donald owns that distinction.

Now, they are expected to become teammates on a defensive line that already includes Byron Young, whom Pro Football Focus ranked as the NFL's ninth-best edge defender last season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But let us not focus solely on the defensive additions.

On offense, the Rams return reigning MVP Matt Stafford, a top-tier offensive line, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, running back Kyren Lacy and head coach Sean McVay, whom most preseason rankings consider the best in football.

Last season, the Rams led the NFL in both yards and points per game. Odds are they will do so again.

It is not unreasonable to argue the Rams enter the season with the NFL's best head coach, play-caller, quarterback, wide receiver, receiving duo, offensive line, defensive player, defensive line, cornerback and cornerback tandem.

Cowherd may have undersold this roster by calling it merely the best of the past decade. You may have to go back to the undefeated 2007 New England Patriots to find a roster this dominant across so many position groups.

The Rams do differ from the Dodgers in a few key ways. They have not won back-to-back championships. More importantly, they have sacrificed more of their future in terms of draft picks and inexpensive contracts because of the constraints of a salary-capped league. Perhaps the better comparison is the 2017-18 Golden State Warriors after signing Kevin Durant.

Those Warriors teams were not built for half a decade of dominance. But while they were together and healthy, no team truly had a chance to compete. I fear that is how the NFL could feel this season.

It is not ideal for the league when torn ACLs and pulled hamstrings become the biggest source of competitive balance. Yet that appears to be the most common argument for someone beating the Rams this season.

To be clear, I am not criticizing the Dodgers or the Rams for loading up. If anything, the criticism belongs elsewhere. Too many franchises have grown comfortable with mediocrity.

While the Rams spent the offseason assembling a super team, much of the NFL stood still, making only modest improvements. That imbalance is frustrating for fans because it sends a troubling message that not every franchise appears to care about winning with the same urgency.

There was a time, not too long ago, when nearly every NFL fan base could convince itself it had a chance to win the Super Bowl in August. Well, not every fan base. Sorry, Jets and Browns fans.

That is no longer the case. As the NFL preseason begins this week, the number of fan bases that can realistically convince themselves they can compete with a roster like the Rams is small.

For a league that prides itself on parity, resembling Major League Baseball in this regard is a problem. The Rams emerging as the NFL's version of the Dodgers, even if only for one season, is not good for the sport.

item.title: ICE asks North Carolina to hold illegal immigrant accused in toddler’s bathtub death
item.description: ICE has filed a detainer against an illegal immigrant accused of leaving his 14-month-old stepchild unattended in a bathtub. The child allegedly drowned, DHS said.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer against a criminal illegal alien who allegedly left a 14-month-old toddler to drown in a bathtub, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

The ICE detainer asks North Carolina officials not to release Angel Israel Deras-Rivas, a Salvadoran national who was arrested Sunday in Garner.

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized the Biden administration's immigration policies, arguing they contributed to the circumstances surrounding the case.

"This criminal illegal alien has been charged with murder and felony child abuse after letting a 14-month-old drown in a bathtub," Mullin said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE

Deras-Rivas, 19, was caring for his stepchild when he allegedly left the toddler unattended in a bathtub filled with water, resulting in the child's death, according to an arrest warrant cited by The Raleigh News & Observer. The incident happened just months after Deras-Rivas married the child's mother in April, the outlet reported.

Immigration officials said Deras-Rivas, identified by DHS as a criminal illegal alien, unlawfully entered the United States through Texas in October 2023 and was released into the country by the Biden administration.

ICE URGES NORTH CAROLINA TO KEEP ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN TRIPLE-FATAL HIT-AND-RUN BEHIND BARS

"That child would still be alive today if it weren’t for the reckless open-border policies of the Biden administration that released this criminal into our country in the first place. ICE is calling on officials in North Carolina to commit to not releasing this killer from jail, and to turn him over to ICE custody so we can get him out of our country."

Immigration officials said ICE filed the detainer with the Wake County Sheriff's Department on the same day Deras-Rivas was arrested.

An ICE detainer typically requests that local law enforcement notify the agency before an individual's release and hold the person for up to 48 additional hours beyond a scheduled release date, allowing ICE agents time to take the individual into federal custody for potential removal proceedings.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Garner Police Department for more information.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs caps huge week for NFL running backs with most lucrative deal from the Detroit Lions
item.description: Jahmyr Gibbs' record $22.5 million-per-year deal caps a historic week for NFL running backs, but Detroit Lions fans want a Super Bowl now.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a big week for NFL running backs stuffing their bank accounts with one big contract after another. And Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs saved the best for last.

Gibbs agreed Thursday evening to a three-year deal worth $67.5 million that includes $51.5 million in guaranteed money. The deal was announced by agent Todd France, who represents Gibbs, on his Instagram account.

Gibbs will be averaging an NFL-high $22.5 million per season on an annual average basis.

FALCONS' BIJAN ROBINSON BECOMES HIGHEST-PAID RUNNING BACK IN NFL HISTORY WITH MASSIVE CONTRACT: REPORT

That's understandable because he has turned the running back spot into a playmaking position at heights not really seen in Detroit since Barry Sanders did his thing in the 1990s.

Gibbs has scored 39 rushing touchdowns in his first three seasons. He also scored 10 more receiving touchdowns. He led the NFL with 20 total TDs from scrimmage in 2024.

The Gibbs deal came hours after Jonathan Taylor agreed to a two-year extension with the Indianapolis Colts that averages $22 million per season.

The Gibbs deal also comes days after Bijan Robinson signed a deal with the Atlanta Falcons that averages $22.25 million per season.

Yes, big week for NFL running backs. All of those players surpassed Saquon Barkley's contract that averages $20.6 million per season and stood as the benchmark for the position since the 2025 offseason.

DETROIT LIONS GREAT FRANK RAGNOW DETAILS HIS ABRUPT RETIREMENT, FAILED COMEBACK ATTEMPT

So, is there any downside to any of this?

For the Detroit Lions, it signals them doing something familiar in that they draft well and pay to keep their own players.

They have now extended Gibbs, Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Penei Sewell, Jameson Williams, Alim McNeill and Kerby Joseph, all good players the team drafted.

The Lions have used that expensive talent to win the NFC North in 2023, ending a 32-year playoff victory drought, advancing to the NFC championship game that postseason, winning a franchise-record 15 games in 2024 and reaching the playoffs again last season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But you know what's missing?

A Super Bowl berth.

A Super Bowl win.

Dan Campbell's team has been outstanding in the draft, developing young talent and winning.

But that drafted and developed talent is playing at a much steeper price now. We're talking over $800 million in total contract commitments for those picks now with the Gibbs deal.

The Lions should be expected to get the Super Bowl championship they are most definitely paying for.

item.title: 'Primetime' star Robert Pattinson shocks fans with Chris Hansen transformation in 'unsettling' trailer
item.description: The trailer for A24's "Primetime" reveals Robert Pattinson's uncanny Chris Hansen transformation, sparking Oscar buzz and true crime debate.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Robert Pattinson left fans doing a double take after debuting his eerie Chris Hansen transformation in A24's "Primetime" trailer.

A24 released the first trailer for "Primetime," the upcoming thriller starring Pattinson as the "To Catch a Predator" host, on Thursday. The film, directed by Lance Oppenheim, follows Hansen as he sets out to make television history in the 2000s.

"To Catch a Predator" was a popular Dateline NBC series hosted by Hansen that used undercover sting operations to confront adults accused of attempting to meet minors for sex before they were arrested by police. Pattinson did truly morph into Hansen for the film in the trailer.

'THE SOCIAL RECKONING' TRAILER DROPS WITH JEREMY STRONG AS ZUCKERBERG IN AARON SORKIN'S FACEBOOK SEQUEL

"What would have happened if I wasn't here," the actor said in the trailer, using some of Hansen's most iconic lines. "You see how this looks, right? At the end of the day, a man must be held accountable for the decisions that he makes. Would you agree? Do you watch television? Well, there is something you should know. I'm Chris Hansen, with Dateline NBC, and you're about to be a part of television history."

It didn't take long for the trailer to set social media ablaze. Fans praised Pattinson's performance, predicted Oscar buzz and declared A24 had another hit on its hands.

"Pattinson is about to get an Oscar nomination for this," one user wrote. "The man cannot miss."

"If there's one thing Pattinson is going to bring to the table, it's a crazy little voice," another user added. "He's had an incredible year; I can't wait for this one."

JESSICA CHASTAIN'S NEW HORROR MOVIE 'OTHER MOMMY' DROPS A TERRIFYING FIRST TRAILER FOR FANS

"This is gonna be so PEAK I cannot wait," one fan wrote.

"A24 somehow took one of the most memeable true-crime shows of all time and turned it into something that feels genuinely unsettling," another said. "September 25th is going to be a problem."

But not everyone was focused on Pattinson's performance. Some viewers were left wondering whether the film would tackle the real-life controversy that brought "To Catch a Predator" to an abrupt end.

"Ok, but why does this trailer make it seem like Hansen is the bad guy?" one user questioned.

"Is the story of why they stopped filming the show in there like about the guy who killed himself when caught," another asked.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"To Catch A Predator" quickly ended after a highly controversial 2006 sting in Texas involving Assistant District Attorney Bill Conradt. Conradt had allegedly communicated online with a decoy posing as a 13-year-old boy but never arrived at the sting house. Instead, police, accompanied by Dateline NBC cameras, went to his home to serve a search warrant. As officers entered the house, Conradt died by suicide.

Although Hansen has maintained that the series simply ran its course after three years, the Conradt case is widely viewed as the event that led to the show's cancellation in 2008.

Pattinson has balanced major studio films with acclaimed auteur projects in recent years. He's appeared in "The Batman," "The Boy and the Heron," "Mickey 17," "Die My Love," "The Drama" and Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey."

He also has several high-profile projects in the pipeline, including "Dune: Part Three," "Here Comes the Flood" and "The Batman: Part II."

item.title: Democratic strategist James Carville says he could become a Republican under one major condition
item.description: Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville revealed the only hypothetical scenario in which he'd join the Republican Party as Hasan Piker and democratic socialists gain ground.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville told Fox News Digital Thursday there is only one unlikely scenario in which he would actually join the Republican Party.

Posed with a hypothetical where Republicans had the policies of former President Bill Clinton from the 1990s and the Democratic Party fully embraced socialism, Carville said, "That’s a fantasy, OK, but, yeah, hypothetically, if I — hypothetically I could fly to the moon — it's about the same chance that that happens.

"Well, if the Democrats went crazy and the Republicans went sane, then I probably would be a Republican," he added. "But I don't see any evidence that there's any possibility that the latter could happen.

"I think it's more likely than not that the Democrats embrace sanity," Carville continued, saying the party’s direction will be determined by Democratic primary voters.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

In recent months, there has been a rising faction of far-left Democratic candidates in multiple states to the point Carville has suggested there be a schism to keep them out of power.

Hasan Piker, a self-described socialist streamer who campaigned with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has emerged as a leading voice on the left as democratic socialists gain ground in elections across the country. 

Piker is known for far-left rhetoric, including previously saying "America deserved 9/11." After widespread criticism, Piker said in an interview he "obviously" did not mean America deserved the attacks and defended the viral quote as a critique of U.S. foreign policy.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," Carville said recently on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing." "If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy."

Speaking to Fox News Digital on Thursday, Carville addressed what would happen if the socialist faction took over the Democratic Party.

"That probably would result in some kind of schism in the party," he reiterated. "I'm going to let Democratic voters determine the direction that party goes in, and if it goes in the direction — which I'm pretty confident it won't — but if it goes in that direction, then I'm going to be 82, OK, fine, go ahead, but not with me.

"Until Democratic voters choose the direction of the party, I'll try to do all I can to help them make the right choice, in my opinion."

JOHN FETTERMAN MAKES IT 'VERY CLEAR' THAT HE'S 'NOT GOING TO BE A REPUBLICAN' DESPITE DEM BACKLASH

Carville's threat to leave the Democratic Party has been mocked by its progressive wing.

"Now James Carville is talking about leaving the party," Piker said during a recent video appearance with El-Sayed. "We got [Pennsylvania Sen.] John Fetterman, James Carville fantasizing about leaving the party. I'm like, 'You're sweetening the deal.' That was really interesting."

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has also stood by Piker after Carville's warning.

"Well, that's not much of a choice," Sanders said of choosing between Piker and Carville. "If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party that I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party."

Fox News' Lindsay Kornick, Hanna Panreck and Nora Moriarty contributed to this report.

item.title: ESPN personality busted on social media for inaccurately trying to promote the SEC's strength of schedule
item.description: ESPN radio host Peter Burns claimed no Big Ten team plays five top-25 coaches poll opponents, but at least seven Big Ten schools actually do.
item.content:encoded:
Well, this isn't going to help ESPN beat the allegations.

It's something of an open secret that ESPN wants the SEC to be the dominant powerhouse in college football. Now that ESPN is the home of most SEC television broadcasts, along with the producer of the SEC Network, it's become abundantly clear that they have a vested interest in promoting the conference and its teams.

The more SEC teams are ranked in the polls, the more "games between ranked teams" they can advertise. The more teams that reach the College Football Playoff, the better for the network. Potentially in terms of future promotion and current ratings. Their advocacy has real meaning, both in terms of fan perception and, as many believe, with the playoff selection committee.

INDIANA'S CURT CIGNETTI ROASTS THE SEC AS ESPN STARTS THEIR PROMOTIONAL CAMPAIGN ALREADY: 'WE DON'T WHINE'

Former Notre Dame quarterback Brady Quinn said as much last season, arguing that the Alabama Crimson Tide were included after a blowout loss to Georgia primarily because ESPN worked so hard, with Greg Sankey and several coaches, to sell the narrative that even reaching the SEC Championship Game was an unimaginable accomplishment. Ignore that non-competitive loss to an awful Florida State team. Kirk Herbstreit went on a tirade during the 2024-25 playoff after Indiana lost to Notre Dame, yet had nothing to say about Alabama's utter obliteration in the 2026 Rose Bowl. As just a few examples.

There's an entire infrastructure of SEC-based promoters and personalities throughout the organization. Paul Finebaum being one of the more obvious examples. But flying under the radar is ESPN radio host and SEC Network studio anchor Peter Burns.

Burns makes no bones about his job: sell the SEC. At all costs. Which, uh, backfired a bit recently when Burns tried to dunk on the Big Ten's schedule based on the preseason coaches poll.

"9 SEC schools play at least 5 of the Top 25 teams in the coaches poll," he posted. "Not a single Big 10 team plays 5. Efficient work."

MISSOURI'S ELI DRINKWITZ BECOMES LATEST SEC COACH TO MAKE RIDICULOUS COMPLAINTS ABOUT BIG TEN SCHEDULES

There's just one problem with that statement and attempted dunk. It's not true.

Not only is there more than one Big Ten team that plays at least five of the top 25 teams in the coaches poll, there's actually seven Big Ten teams that do.

Ohio State plays Texas, Iowa, Indiana, USC, Oregon and Michigan. That's six teams.

Michigan plays Oklahoma, Iowa, Penn State, Indiana, Oregon and Ohio State. That's also six.

LANE KIFFIN MAKES RIDICULOUS EXCUSES FOR SEC'S POOR RECENT PERFORMANCE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

USC plays Oregon, Washington, Penn State, Ohio State and Indiana. That's five.

Nebraska plays Indiana, Oregon, Washington, Ohio State and Iowa. That's five.

Minnesota plays Washington, Michigan, Iowa, Indiana and Penn State. That's also five.

Washington plays USC, Iowa, Penn State, Indiana and Oregon. Five again.

Purdue plays Notre Dame, Washington, Penn State, Iowa and Indiana. Five teams.

USC would have six, but Notre Dame backed out of playing their traditional rivalry game early in the season, only to agree to do that same thing in 2030, for some reason. But the point remains, if you're going to try to claim SEC superiority based on the coaches poll, of all things, at least be accurate about it.

Obviously the job of the SEC Network is to promote the SEC. They're not covering it objectively, or even pretending to. But the problem is that ESPN has an inordinate amount of influence with the College Football Playoff. And this type of inaccuracy and reliance on preseason polls is exactly the type of snowball effect that fans of other conferences complain about.

SEC proponents brag about the number of preseason ranked games, then when some of those ranked teams come up well short of expectations, like, say 2025 Florida or Auburn, there's no adjustment later on. Once an SEC team is ranked in any poll at any point in the season, they are forever a ranked team. Both conferences have tough schedules with good teams. At this point, that's all that matters.

item.title: Tom Rahill captures 96 Burmese pythons in 10 days to win 2026 Florida Python Challenge
item.description: Tom Rahill captured 96 Burmese pythons in Everglades National Park in just 10 days, but his real mission involved a veteran and a 17-foot snake.
item.content:encoded:
It was a bad week to be a Burmese python.

Tom Rahill removed 96 of the invasive snakes from the Everglades in just 10 days — more than enough to leave the rest of the field in the swamp dust.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

Rahill was named the ultimate grand prize winner of the 2026 Florida Python Challenge on Wednesday, earning $10,000 for capturing more snakes than any other competitor during the 10-day event.

And apparently, once he got rolling, there was no stopping him.

Rahill founded SwampApes, a Broward County organization that takes military veterans suffering from PTSD on python hunts in the Florida wetlands, in 2017. He said his primary goal during this year’s competition was to help one of those veterans land a monster.

"I was on a mission to get one of our veterans a big snake," Rahill said during a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission meeting in Panama City. "I did it. And we wrestled this thing. That was the mission. To get him a big snake — it was a 17-foot female. The veteran was just over the moon."

Mission accomplished.

FLORIDA FISHERMAN USES SPEARGUN TO HOLD OFF THREE ATTACKING SHARKS DURING DESTIN DIVE

Rahill then turned his attention toward piling up as many snakes as possible.

"I went deeper in the Glades, and that’s when I found those 96," he said.

All 96 of Rahill’s pythons were captured in Everglades National Park.

The annual Florida Python Challenge drew 907 participants from 30 states, Canada and Vietnam this year. Competitors collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons from eight designated hunting areas across South Florida between July 10 and July 19.

The competition awards prizes in professional, novice and military divisions, along with the $10,000 grand prize for the most pythons captured overall.

Christina Kraus won the professional division with 36 snakes, while defending grand prize winner Taylor Stanberry finished second with 34 and earned $1,500.

Stanberry made history last year when she removed 60 pythons to become the first woman ever to win the competition. Her 2025 haul included 33 females and 27 males.

You can watch her interview with OutKick Outdoors here:

Rahm Levinson earned the professional division’s longest-python prize after capturing a snake measuring 16 feet, 5 inches.

The contest is not just about cash prizes or bragging rights. It's also about conservation.

Burmese pythons are native to Southeast Asia and have devastated native wildlife populations since becoming established in the Everglades. The invasive predators have contributed to declines among raccoons, opossums, bobcats, foxes, marsh rabbits and cottontail rabbits.

They are also remarkably difficult to locate because of their camouflage and secretive behavior. Conservative estimates place the python population in the Everglades region in the tens of thousands.

The challenge was moved to the summer in recent years to coincide with python hatching season, allowing hunters to remove young snakes before they have an opportunity to spread or prey on native wildlife.

Sarah Funck of the FWC told the Naples Daily News there is no single solution to Florida’s python problem but said every removal matters.

The elimination of even one python, she said, "is a win for Florida’s native wildlife."

In that case, Rahill delivered Florida 96 wins in just 10 days.

item.title: UNLV coach Dan Mullen throws dig at former employer, Florida, but numbers tell a complicated story
item.description: Dan Mullen shared theories on his Florida firing with Paul Finebaum, claiming the Gators would have made the College Football Playoff three times.
item.content:encoded:
Let's rewind the clocks back to November 7, 2020.

The Florida Gators, being coached by former championship-winning offensive coordinator Dan Mullen, just knocked off bitter rival Georgia to take a stranglehold of the SEC East.

It's the first time in four seasons that the Gators have gotten the best of the Bulldogs, and if they can just hold serve against a relatively weak back half of their schedule, they will stamp their tickets to Atlanta to take on the Alabama Crimson Tide for a chance to make the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history.

ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026

Just over a year later, the Gators would fire Mullen, kickstarting a coaching search that would ultimately lead them to Louisiana head coach Billy Napier.

How did it all go so wrong so fast?

Mullen has some theories, and he shared his insight while discussing the end of his Florida tenure with Paul Finebaum earlier this week.

"We won a lot of games," Mullen said. "But you know what? In today’s world, when you’re when you’re at premier schools, you expect to win. At Florida, they expect championships... that's the standard."

He's not wrong.

Florida has hired seven coaches since 1990, and without counting their newest hire, Jon Sumrall, who doesn't even have a single game as a Gator under his belt, every coach who has failed to win a national or SEC championship in Gainesville has been shown the door.

That includes Mullen, who was 34-15 at the time of his firing.

A nearly 70% winning percentage hardly seems like a fireable offense, but as Mullen said, the goal is to win championships at Florida.

"We got to an SEC championship game, fell a couple points short to Alabama," said Mullen. "But our standard from the day I got there was championships. We weren’t able to come through, even though we fell a couple points short on on winning the SEC Championship, and going to compete for national championships.

"And I think maybe if the Playoff era was around, I think three out of my four years, we would have made the College Football Playoff. Maybe that would have looked a little bit different back then with the resume, of keeping me around a little bit longer to try to try to go win that national title. But hey, it is what it is. Probably hasn’t gone as well there since I left, it doesn’t seem like."

That last line is the kicker, and reveals just how much resentment Mullen still holds for his former employer.

Once again, Mullen isn't entirely wrong when he says Florida is worse off without him, and he's also spot on when he says they would have made a 12-team Playoff each of his first three seasons.

But Mullen also wasn't fired for his first three seasons. He was fired for what was coming in the next three seasons.

I mentioned at the start of the article that Mullen and the Gators were waltzing to the SEC Championship Game a little over a year before he was fired, but what happened in between the 2020 Georgia win and an overtime loss to Missouri in 2021 that led to his ousting?

Well, there's the infamous "Shoe Game," in which the Gators lost at home as a nearly three touchdown favorite against LSU, thanks in large part to cornerback Marco Wilson launching a Tigers player's shoe 20 yards downfield after a third down stop in a tie ball game.

SMU HEAD COACH RHETT LASHLEE POURS GASOLINE ON FIRE, DISPARAGES SUN BELT'S CLAIM TO CFP BERTH

Mullen made him a team captain the very next week for the SEC title game against Bama, highlighting a lack of accountability that would ultimately doom the former Gators head coach.

From the loss to LSU until his firing in 2021, Mullen went 2-9 against Power 5 opponents, not exactly a sign of things trending in the right direction.

Things weren't much better off the field, either, as Mullen's recruiting classes steadily dipped after each passing season, culminating in a class that was ranked outside the top-20 at the time of his firing.

It would have been the worst recruiting class for a sitting Florida coach since they started tracking those things back in the early 2000s, which includes coaches like Jim McElwain and Ron Zook.

Those guys aren't remembered too fondly in Gainesville and that's company no Florida coach wants to be associated with.

But, if we are being honest, cracks were starting to form in the Mullen regime long before his ill-fated 2021 season.

2020 is looked back on as a season that could have been for the Gators, but it had nothing to do with the offense.

That side of the ball was rocking and rolling, averaging nearly 40 points per game and featuring future NFL draft picks like quarterback Kyle Trask, wide receiver Kadarius Toney, and tight end Kyle Pitts.

As it turns out, football is about more than just offense, and the defense was downright putrid in 2020, giving up nearly 31 points per game and ranking 83rd in the country in total defense.

Mullen had the chance to make a change following the season, but chose to keep defensive coordinator Todd Grantham employed, and it's here that we find another fatal flaw with Mullen's time at Florida: loyalty.

Loyalty, in and of itself, is an admirable quality to have, but as a football coach, when it's time to let someone go, it doesn't matter how close you are to them personally.

WHAT DOES A REALISTICALLY SUCCESSFUL FIRST YEAR LOOK LIKE FOR HEAD COACH LANE KIFFIN AT LSU?

Guys like Grantham and offensive line coach John Hevesy continued to underperform both on the field and on the recruiting trail season after season, but they were never let go until athletic director Scott Stricklin forced Mullen's hand in late 2021, mere weeks before Mullen himself was fired.

Translation: Mullen anchored himself to his buddies, and they ultimately ended up sinking him.

Mullen's point about Florida making an extended College Football Playoff each of his three full seasons there is well taken, but I'm reminded of his own words echoing in my ears about the standard being championships.

Yes, the Gators would have been squarely in the CFP in 2018, 2019, and 2020.

Then what?

For those who aren't aware, Dan Mullen was 4-7 against top 10 teams during his tenure at Florida, and while that isn't James Franklin levels of abysmal, it does highlight that a 12-team Playoff likely would have gone similarly for Mullen than it did for Franklin.

Statistically, Mullen had less than a 50/50 shot of beating a "Playoff-caliber team" while coaching the Gators, meaning once he got to the big dance, odds are he would have petered out before even reaching the semifinals.

I could go on and on about why Mullen is misguided at best in his attempts to whitewash his tenure at Florida, but I'll leave you with this.

As a Gator fan, I have constantly heard people during the Billy Napier era crow about how wrong Florida was to have ever fired Mullen, and I wince in anger every time.

Not because they're correct, but because of how off they really are.

Firing Dan Mullen in 2021 was the right move for all the reasons I listed above, and then some.

Firing Dan Mullen to hire an incompetent coach like Napier was the wrong move.

That's the long and short of it.

Being a better coach than Billy Napier, who was statistically the worst Florida has had since World War II, is a low bar to clear.

Programs with championship aspirations, as Mullen so deftly pointed out, shouldn't be scared of pulling the plug on someone who can't get over the hump.

Stop letting "good" be the enemy of "great."

Georgia famously fired Mark Richt following the 2015 season, a season in which the Bulldogs won ten games.

Richt was a two-time SEC champion, had six seasons in which he finished in the AP top-ten, and compiled a 145-51 record.

By most conceivable metrics, Richt was infinitely more successful than Mullen as a head coach, yet the Bulldogs jettisoned him for failing to live up to the championship expectations of a program like Georgia.

Mind you, Georgia had not won a national championship in 35 years at that point, more than double the "drought" that Florida was going through when they pulled the plug on Mullen.

Yet, no one chastises Georgia for this because they ended up hiring Kirby Smart, a coach who has taken them to heights even the most optimistic Bulldog fan likely couldn't have dreamed of.

Florida fired their "Mark Richt" but failed to hire their "Kirby Smart."

It happens to every program in America that has expectations similar to that of a Florida or Georgia (hello, Penn State).

I will say it again: Florida was correct in firing Dan Mullen.

The fact that they whiffed on his immediate predecessor doesn't change that, and I will stand on that hill for the rest of time.

item.title: Country star Hannah Dasher says famous, married celebrity once slid into her DMs

item.content:encoded:
Country singer Hannah Dasher revealed that a famous, married celebrity once slid into her direct messages on social media, but explained her Christian faith has kept her from taking shortcuts in the music industry.

During a recent appearance on the "Like a Farmer" podcast, the 40-year-old musician was asked about the "weirdest" DM that she has ever received.

"Well, I don't know that I could share it because they're famous and married," Dasher said, without naming the individual. "So let me think of another one."

ELLA LANGLEY GOES VIRAL WITH PASSIONATE COMMENTS ABOUT HER CHRISTIAN FAITH, GOD, LOVE AND RELIGION

"I could have gone on some pretty big tours, you know, if I wasn't a Christian," she added with a smile. "Golly, the weirdest DM that I've gotten. I guess that would be it, right? I don't know."

"Oh, I think about that one."

Raised near Savannah, Georgia, Dasher has previously said that she grew up on '90s country music. After graduating from college, she moved to Nashville, Tennessee to pursue a career in country music. Dasher has previously said that she worked selling boats and outboard motors at Bass Pro Shops to support herself before being fired for writing songs while on the job.

In 2013, she landed her first publishing deal with BMG Chrysalis and later signed with Sony/ATV Music Publishing in partnership with Jaren Johnston of The Cadillac Three. Dasher's first major break as a songwriter came in 2017, when Brad Paisley recorded her co-written song "Go to Bed Early" for his "Love and War" album, marking her first cut for a major label.

LAINEY WILSON SAYS CITY PEOPLE HAVE WRONG VIEW OF COUNTRY TOWNS AS SHE DEFENDS HER 'BLUE COLLAR' ROOTS

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Dasher launched her viral TikTok cooking series, "Stand By Your Pan," where she mixes Southern recipes with country music and comedy. Dasher signed a recording deal with Sony Music Nashville in 2021 and released her debut EP, "The Half Record," which featured songs including "Leave This Bar" and "Girls Call the Shots."

That same year, she was named one of CMT's Next Women of Country and made multiple appearances performing at the Grand Ole Opry.

She has since said that Sony "pulled the plug" on her recording deal shortly after the EP's release, leaving her to continue her career independently.

SHANIA TWAIN SAYS SHE'S FINALLY 'GETTING IT RIGHT' IN HER 60S AFTER STARTING LIFE ‘ON THE TOUGH SIDE’

While speaking on the "Like a Farmer" podcast, Dasher candidly reflected on her career setback.

"I think losing my record deal was a huge humbling that needed to occur in me and it was the last thing that I thought was ever going to happen," she said. "But the devil will steal your confidence when moments like that happen."

ELLA LANGLEY'S FAITH AND AUTHENTICITY FUEL RECORD-BREAKING RISE, EXPERTS SAY

"And so I just had to remind myself that I didn't move to this town for anybody but me," she continued. "And you know that I have people that love me and depended on me and I just knew that I needed to um to get out of that lull and to start writing songs again."

Dasher explained that taking some time off from songwriting to pen her cookbook "Stand By Your Pan: 100 Easy and Affordable Comfort Food Recipes So Good They'll Hurt People's Feelin's," which was published in March was a "great way to kind of get those wheels turning again."

SINGER ZACH TOP SLAMS MODERN COUNTRY MUSIC, SAYS IT LACKS 'SOUL'

"And so I've kind of been out of the songwriting thing for a couple of years because of this, and now I'm back into it and I caught the fever again, if you will," she said. "I'm so excited to be working on new music and just to be growing this thing."

"And this time it's just so much more free," Dasher continued. "I don't have any rules over me that I feel like I'm having to write for, or that I can't do this or I can't say this. I'm just making this as authentically Hannah as it can be. Just real."

Dasher also shared her thoughts on the current state of country music, which has recently experienced a massive surge in popularity.

"I think country is always trending," she said. "I knew this '90s thing would come back around."

item.title: Best bet for the Carolina Panthers vs Arizona Cardinals 2026 NFL Pro Football Hall of Fame Game
item.description: Kenny Pickett starts for Carolina against Carson Beck and Arizona in the Pro Football Hall of Fame game, with coaching continuity favoring the Panthers.
item.content:encoded:
My fellow Americans, our long national nightmare is over. The NFL returns Thursday, Aug. 6, with the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame game between the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio, at 8 p.m. ET.

Carolina and Arizona are playing Thursday because Panthers and Cardinals greats, Panthers LB Luke Kuechly and Cardinals WR Larry Fitzgerald, are members of the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, along with Drew Brees, Roger Craig and Adam Vinatieri.

As per Hall of Fame Game tradition, neither team will play its starters Thursday. There is a sharp way to handicap the NFL preseason. Between listening to coachspeak during training camp and getting a clue about the depth chart and player rotations, then doing a deep dive into the positional competitions.

CARDINALS OPEN TRAINING CAMP WEDNESDAY AS ARGUABLY NFL'S MOST DEPRESSING TEAM

However, I’m celebrating the return of football the best way I know how and just straight up gambling here. Albeit I’ll show my math, so to speak, on how I landed on my bet. With that in mind, here’s my look for the Panthers-Cardinals Hall of Fame Game Thursday.

The three things I look for when betting the NFL preseason include coaching continuity, roster depth, and quarterback experience, and Carolina has an edge in two of those departments.

There will be a learning curve for Arizona under rookie head coach Mike LaFleur. Whereas this is Panthers head coach Canales’ third season on the job, and he’s had the same offensive and defensive coordinators for the first two seasons.

PANTHERS DEFENSE TAKES MAJOR HIT AS STAR PASS RUSHER SUFFERS MAJOR INJURY ON FIRST DAY OF CAMP: REPORTS

Obviously, both teams will be playing guys who may or may not make the regular-season roster. But the Panthers who were on the team last year will have an edge Thursday because they won't have to learn a new system.

Carolina will start QB Kenny Pickett in the Hall of Fame Game, while the Cardinals are giving third-string rookie QB Carson Beck the nod on Thursday. While Pickett is a bad starting quarterback and on his fourth team in five NFL seasons, he is 16-11 as a starter and a first-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, compared to Beck, who was taken in the third round.

Furthermore, Pickett is more mobile, and I like backing the more mobile quarterbacks in the preseason. Offenses are less buttoned-up, and teams rarely have their starters on the field, so I want my quarterback to make plays off-structure.

Panthers rookie QB Haynes King will take over for Pickett eventually and Beck will turn the offense over to second-year Cardinals QB Kedon Slovis. For what it's worth, I'll take King over Slovis. Both went undrafted, but King was the 2025 ACC Player of the Year for Georgia Tech, and Slovis won zero college football awards.

Two of Carolina's starters, DE Nic Scourton and rookie WR Chris Brazzell II, suffered season-ending injuries during the first two weeks of training camp. The injuries hurt the Panthers' depth heading into the regular season, but neither team is playing its starters Thursday.

That said, Canales might push his backups harder and play the second-stringers longer, knowing he is already down two starters. I.e., there is more motivation for Carolina's coaching staff to use more regular-season stuff.

Maybe I'm just talking myself into a bet because football is back and I've been waiting for this day since the Super Bowl. Nonetheless, I'm not going to not bet the NFL Pro Football Hall of Fame Game. After all, it's tradition.

item.title: Trump signs executive orders targeting birthright citizenship, birth tourism after Supreme Court setback
item.description: The orders deny visas to those entering the country to give birth, and Trump promised "very big crackdowns" on organized birth tourism operations.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Thursday signed two executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and birth tourism, saying his administration is taking a new approach after what he called a "very unfortunate" Supreme Court ruling.

"We're making adjustments because it's very unfair," Trump said. "They're building businesses around birthright citizenship. That's not the way it was supposed to work. It's a disgrace. They're buying their way in, and we're not going to let it happen."

The moves come after the Supreme Court blocked Trump's earlier executive order seeking to limit automatic birthright citizenship under the 14th Amendment.

BIRTH TOURISM CRACKDOWN EXPANDS AS HOUSE CHAIRMAN RAISES CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY CASE

White House officials said the new directives rely on existing executive and immigration authorities and are intended to narrow eligibility for automatic citizenship in certain cases while cracking down on foreigners who travel to the United States to give birth.

White House deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller said the first order expands the categories of people the administration considers ineligible for birthright citizenship, including "alien enemies of the United States, members of foreign terrorist organizations, and large categories of people who lobby and act on behalf of foreign governments."

Miller said the second order was issued "for the first time ever in American history to ban birth tourism." He said the administration will deny visas to people who seek to enter the United States "to have a child, to make that child an automatic citizen" as well as those who organize such trips. 

Citing Section 215(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, Miller called birth tourism "by definition, a fraud on the American system" and "a fraud against the American government."

TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP FIGHT COMES ROARING BACK WITH ‘INVADERS’ PLAY AFTER KAVANAUGH ROADMAP

Asked how the administration plans to enforce the order, Trump said, "We're cracking down very big, very big, big crackdowns. ... This will give us the right to do it in a much more forceful manner." 

When asked whether the orders would survive court challenges, Trump replied, "I think it will."

Will Scharf, White House staff secretary, said the orders target organized birth tourism operations through visa denials and law enforcement, arguing the administration was relying on "legally validated means" that do not conflict with the Supreme Court's ruling.

The White House had not yet released the text of the executive orders as of publication time.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional comment.

item.title: Senator Eric Schmitt joins Dakich, fires back against Senator Hawley over Title IX claims
item.description: Sen. Eric Schmitt says the Protect College Sports Act does not preempt Title IX, pushing back on concerns raised by Riley Gaines and Josh Hawley.
item.content:encoded:
Much ado has been made about the Protect College Sports Act, a bipartisan bill that aims to create a framework to stabilize NIL in the current landscape of the NCAA.

Though there are plenty of proponents on both sides of the political aisle, there are still many who have taken exception with some of the perceived loopholes in the bill, particularly those which pertain to Title IX.

A few of those opposed to the bill in its current format include OutKick's very own Riley Gaines and Missouri senator Josh Hawley, both of whom voiced their displeasure on their respective X accounts recently.

TED CRUZ URGES SENATE TO STAY IN WASHINGTON UNTIL PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT PASSES THIS WEEK

Another Senator from the Show Me State, Eric Schmitt, was on Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich on Thursday, and he made sure to quell any fears of the PCSA preempting Title IX's authority.

When asked by Dakich about Gaines and Sen. Hawley's reservations with regard to the latest bill, Schmitt didn't hold back.

"No, I couldn't agree," the Senator said. "I think a further review or a deeper look into the language would show that that's just not true at all. There's specific language in there that protects civil rights laws of states. There's no preemption there. And it specifically says this doesn't change or modify title nine at all."

Sen. Schmitt told Dakich that there's a lot of momentum behind the bill in Washington and they are looking to make a move "as soon as this weekend," presumably to get something done before the Senate's recess.

PRESIDENT TRUMP PUSHES LAWMAKERS ON LEGISLATION AS 'PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT' HANGS ON BY A THREAD

The sense of urgency comes not just from the impending recess, but from the fact that NIL and college athletics in general has been out of whack for years now.

"This is a really important bill to kind of calm the chaos that we've got in college sports with unlimited transfers and 27-year-olds competing against 17-year-olds," Sen. Schmitt said.

It's worth noting that Sen. Hawley, in addition to a few other Republicans including Senator and former Auburn head coach Tommy Tuberville, have filed an amendment Thursday trying to stop the current bill from overriding state women's sports laws.

Time will tell which GOP Senators will win out, but it's safe to say the battleground that is the PCSA won't be cooling down anytime soon.
